newsitem.title: USA: Intellicall sees improved Q4 results.
newsitem.headline: Intellicall sees improved Q4 results.

text.p: Intellicall Inc said on Friday it expects results in the fourth quarter of 1996 to be a "significant improvement" over previous periods this year.

The company said the expected improvement is due to both domestic and foreign sales, improved margins from the company's new AstraTel 2 line powered payphone, continued cost reductions, and lower interest costs.

The company posted a third-quarter net loss of $2.8 million, or $0.35 per share, on revenues of $26.3 million compared with a net loss was $1.9 million, or $.24 per share, on revenues of $19.2 million the same period last year.

Domestic demand for payphones has been weak this year as payphone owners waited for the outcome of Federal Communications Commission deliberations on competition and dial-around compensation, the company said. Because recent FCC activity was favorable to private payphone operators, the company said the operators should see better cash flows in 1997.
William Hunt, Intellicall's chairman and chief executive, said the 1996 financial results were mixed.

"Intellicall's service businesses have made progress in all areas, and despite increased competition have basically held the line on absolute profits. However, our efforts toward regaining profitability in 1996 have been hurt by the lack of industry demand in the U.S. market, and softer than expected sales internationally," Hunt said.
Hunt also said that the company has continued improving its operational cost structure and expects spending to continue declining for the foreseeable future.
The company said Hunt joined other senior managers in buying 100,000 shares of outstanding Intellicall stock this week.
